title: Zelensky visits Washington, meets Biden and addresses Congress
body:
On 21 December 2022, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky travelled to Washington, D.C. It was his first trip abroad since Russia launched its full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022. The Kyiv Independent, citing the Associated Press, reported on 20 December that two congressional sources and one other person had said the visit was being prepared, and that it could still be cancelled at the last minute over security concerns.

Planned events included a meeting with President Joe Biden at the White House and an address to a joint meeting of the US Congress. The visit coincided with US preparations to send Patriot surface-to-air missiles to Ukraine. Associated Press coverage reported that the trip followed a phone call between Biden and Zelensky on 11 December, and that Biden said it was an honour to be by Zelensky's side on what was the 300th day of the invasion.

Speaker Nancy Pelosi described the joint session as having a special focus on democracy, and the White House said the speech would show strong bipartisan support for Ukraine. Several Republicans had criticised the level of US support, and Republicans were due to take control of the House in January 2023. On the same day Washington announced a 1.85 billion dollar aid package.
